_meta.status: DRAFT — medic review required. Values tagged TUNE are gameplay tuning anchors, not clinical constants.
rules: Conditions modify true physiological state per tick. They never set displayed values directly.
findings are returned only when the player performs that assessment action on that region.
spawns: conditions this one can create later (probability, delay, trigger).
generatorReady: false until a medic has reviewed and the engine models every effect listed.

infectionModel.description: Generic engine object. Every infection is an instance of this with a source, organism profile, and load.

fields.organismProfile: weights 0-1 across: gramPositive, MRSA, gramNegative, pseudomonas, anaerobes, atypical, neisseria, toxinProducing
fields.needsSourceControl: true for abscess, empyema, fecal contamination, necrotizing infection, perforation — antibiotics only SLOW these, they never cure. Source control happens at the hospital (simulated in the outcome projection).

infectionModel.antibioticEffect: growth × (1 − matchScore). matchScore = weighted overlap of drug.coverage (0-3, normalized) with organismProfile. Wrong-spectrum drug ≈ no effect. Logged: time-to-first-antibiotic, appropriateness of coverage.
infectionModel.allergy: If the history card lists penicillin anaphylaxis: penicillins high reaction risk; cephalosporins ~1-2%; carbapenems <1% (TUNE). Reaction = the anaphylaxis condition.
infectionModel.iatrogenicRisk: Skipping BSI/gloves, no skin prep before IV/IO, an IO through a dirty/burned site, or reusing contaminated gear adds wound or line_related infection seeds (small load, shows in the outcome projection).

sepsisModel.description: Driven by total infection load + host response. Stages escalate as load crosses thresholds (TUNE).

treatmentResponses.crystalloid_30mL_per_kg: transiently raises MAP; reassess lung sounds (overload → pulmonary edema)
treatmentResponses.norepinephrine: first-line vasopressor for MAP <65 after fluids
treatmentResponses.early_antibiotics: each hour of delay worsens projected mortality (TUNE ~ +4–8%/h in shock)
treatmentResponses.hydrocortisone: only for vasopressor-dependent shock or known adrenal insufficiency

conditions.name: Sternal fracture
conditions.teachingPoint: The sternum itself is rarely the killer. What's behind it (heart, aorta) is. Get a 12-lead and monitor.

conditions.name: Blunt cardiac injury (myocardial contusion)

effects.rhythm: random from [sinus_tach, PVCs, new_RBBB, afib, VT, VF] weighted toward benign (TUNE)

conditions.teachingPoint: Treat arrhythmias per ACLS. No field fix: monitor, defib pads on, trauma center.

conditions.name: Flail chest

inspect: paradoxical chest wall segment moving IN on inspiration

dangers: Overzealous crystalloid worsens underlying pulmonary contusion

conditions.name: Penetrating thoracoabdominal wound
conditions.description: Any penetrating wound below the nipple line (front) or scapular tip (back): assume BOTH chest and abdomen are injured.

inspect: stab/GSW wound below the nipple line or scapular tip

conditions.name: Traumatic diaphragmatic rupture with herniation

effects.gastric_distension: tracked; rises with BVM overventilation, crying/air swallowing, positive pressure

stages.notes: may be subtle or delayed hours to years

patient: shortness of breath, worse lying flat

traps: NEEDLE DECOMPRESSION into a herniated stomach: gas escapes (brief improvement, possibly) but punctures the stomach → spawns hollow_viscus_perforation_thoracic_contamination (gastric). Logged as an iatrogenic injury unless the clinical picture was indistinguishable from tension pneumo (the FTO explains why).
Finger thoracostomy: feeling bowel/stomach in the pleural space instead of air = diagnosis. Do not dig further.
Pneumatic devices / PASG / tight abdominal binding increase intra-abdominal pressure → more herniation.
conditions.teachingPoint: Hear bowel sounds in the chest = gut in the chest. Decompress the STOMACH (OG tube), not the chest. Trauma center, surgery.

conditions.name: Herniated stomach/colon perforation with pleural contamination

organismProfile._note: acid = chemical pleuritis first; lower bacterial load

effects.on_scene_visible_change: minimal in the first hour — SIRS/sepsis develops over HOURS (see outcome projection)

smell: fecal odor from the chest wound (penetrating fecal variant)

conditions.gore: Clinical setting shows contaminated drainage. Reduced setting desaturates and abstracts it.
conditions.teachingPoint: You can't fix this in the field. Win by recognizing it, early broad antibiotics on long transports, not making it worse, and the right destination.

conditions.name: Esophageal perforation → mediastinitis

patient: severe chest/back pain that started after violent vomiting

traps: Giving PO meds (aspirin, oral glucose, charcoal) leaks more into the mediastinum
conditions.teachingPoint: Vomiting followed by tearing chest pain plus subQ air = Boerhaave until proven otherwise. NPO, antibiotics, surgery-capable center.

conditions.name: Urosepsis
conditions.patientProfile: elderly, nursing home, indwelling catheter, diabetic

thermometer: may be HYPOthermic in the elderly

conditions.teachingPoint: Altered elderly patient with normal vitals at rest still needs a temp, a glucose and a lactate.

conditions.name: Meningococcal sepsis

spawns_infection._tag: TUNE — fastest killer in the library

inspect_skin: non-blanching petechial → purpuric rash spreading over minutes

conditions.crewSafety: Droplet precautions: surgical mask on patient + N95/mask for the crew. Missing it is logged as a crew exposure.
conditions.teachingPoint: The rash spreading while you watch is the clock. Antibiotics within minutes if the transport is long.

conditions.name: Necrotizing fasciitis

patient: pain out of proportion to how it looks

conditions.teachingPoint: Pain out of proportion plus crepitus = surgical emergency.

outcomeProjection.description: After handoff, the engine fast-forwards a coarse hospital course (0-72 h) from the final state + event log. Deterministic per seed. The FTO narrates it in the debrief.
outputs_examples: Feculent empyema at 18 h; thoracotomy + washout; survived ICU stay — your ertapenem at 14 min cut projected septic shock risk.
Admitted with septic shock; antibiotics first given at the ED, 52 min after your contact — FTO notes long transport without antibiotics.
Line infection at the IO site (non-sterile placement).
outcomeProjection.rule: Hospital events are summarized, never played. They reflect field decisions, not luck alone (realism dial controls randomness).

equipmentAdditions: OG and NG tubes + lube + 60 mL catheter-tip syringe (gastric decompression)
Surgical masks / N95 / gowns (droplet + contact precautions)
